problem:
Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ given below. Find $det(A)-det({B}^{T}).$

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{2} & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 2.5 & 0.21 \\ 0 & 2 & 0.1 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}].
$$

feedback.problem: Given that $B=2I$, where $I$ is the $3\times 3$ identity matrix, what is the value of $det(B)?$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, notice that

$$
\begin{aligned}2I & =2[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a diagonal matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot 2\cdot 2=8.\end{aligned}
$$
